gen-fs-expose-gf-sofia-sans: Sofia Sans reads like tall cut stencil pieces, rounded and unmodulated, with open sides on every curve. And Expose, compressed and striking, keeps capitals barely taller than its lowercase, a tight, hurried cadence.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Editorial and commanding, Quilon swells and thins with real confidence. Noto Sans Armenian fills its lowercase tall and opens its round letters wide, so extended text moves along without snagging.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Editorial in tone, Quilon carries the mild stroke variation of a dip pen used gently. Yet Noto Sans Bamum drops the variation entirely, its clean curves ending before they turn inward and every lowercase counter wide.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Editorial and commanding, Quilon shows a modest, readable shift in weight across every curve of its tall letters. Noto Sans Cuneiform, plain sans with bead-like lowercase, rewards a generous size.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Sharp editorial swagger: Quilon puts moderate stroke contrast around large open counters in its tall a. Quilon earns its keep big and short, while Noto Sans Grantha never snags.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew reads with a dominant midsection that swallows the line's height and wide gaps between curve ends and stems. Beneath Quilon, long paragraphs run briskly and clear.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Large open counters give Quilon its editorial command. Noto Sans Kannada, plain sans with s curves open wide at both ends and a gentle bump up to capitals, makes paragraphs feel approachable.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Noto Sans Mandaic keeps its lowercase rising close to capitals, with curvy sans-serif letters that feel unclamped. Following Quilon, with its quiet stroke modulation, running text feels loose and unhurried.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Quilon draws its stems only a shade heavier than their connecting arms, giving big open counters an editorial feel. Noto Sans Ogham, sans-serif with tall bodies, reads boldly across many lines.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Open curves, clear gaps and lowercase filling most of the height make long text go down smoothly. Noto Sans Tagbanwa delivers that beneath Quilon, whose thin strokes are only slightly lighter than its thick ones.
